note: Description taken from Hill's 1925 original description of Eutermes exitiosus (in English), including the alate, soldier and worker; type locality Ludlow, Western Australia, also collected at Pinjarra, Albany, Bunbury, Perth, South Australia and Victoria. The author states that its soldier is conspecific with the specimens Silvestri (1909) referred to E. fumipennis, while the type locality of E. fumipennis is 'New Holland' with no specimen available for comparison. The original is in English and the BHL scan was OCR'd, with occasional misread hyphens and measurement digits (e.g. the hyphen ¬), restored here from context; values that cannot be determined are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A large species: alate with wings 25.00—26.50 mm, but only 6.50—7.00 mm without wings; soldier body length 3.00—3.75 mm, head short and broad, widest in the middle, posterior margin broadly rounded, nasus slightly thick and shorter than the rest of the head, antennae 13-segmented; head capsule deep chestnut-brown with a pale median line running back from the middle of the head, the base of the nasus dark and the tip reddish. The soldier and worker are difficult to separate from E. graveolus and the alate is needed.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep chestnut-brown, postclypeus, labrum, antennae, thorax, legs and venter buff to yellow-ochre; wing stubs mummy brown; abdominal tergites yellow-ochre, much tinged with brown; wing bases mummy brown, fading towards the tip, the anterior margin yellow-ochre. Head medium-sized, depressed behind the postclypeus, the posterior margin broadly rounded, bristles moderate. Compound eyes large (length 0.342—0.375 mm, width 0.400—0.450 mm) and prominent, 0.085 mm from the lower margin of the head; ocelli very large, broadly oval (0.102×0.153 mm); frontal marks small but distinct, linear, forked anteriorly. Postclypeus large, less than half as long as wide (0.255×0.630 mm); anteclypeus transparent, about one third of the length of the postclypeus. Labrum small, rather bristly. Antennae 15-segmented, long and slightly thick. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, anterior margin upturned and slightly notched, with two deep impressions on each side (one at the anterolateral corner, one deeper between it and the midline), the sides narrowing abruptly towards the posterior margin. Wings very large, the membrane densely bristled; fore wing cubitus with about 6 branches, hind wing with about 8, the terminal branches occasionally forked 1—2 times. Legs long and slightly thick (hairy). Abdomen large and broad, the end broadly rounded, bristles very dense; cerci medium-sized. Measurements: body length (with wings) 25.00—26.50 mm; without wings 6.50—7.00 mm; head length (to the end of the labrum) 1.42 mm; head length (to the frontoclypeal suture) 0.80 mm; head width 1.19—1.25 mm; antennal length 2.00 mm; pronotum length 0.74 mm, width 1.34 mm; fore wing length 14.50 mm, width 4.00 mm; hind wing length 13.75 mm, width 4.20 mm; hind tibia length 1.48 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule deep chestnut-brown (as in the alate), the base of the nasus darker and the tip reddish, with a pale median line running back from the middle of the head; anterior half of the pronotum concolorous with the head; antennae, rest of the thorax and abdominal tergites Dresden brown; sternites slightly paler, legs paler still. Cephalic bristles very few, head short and broad, widest in the middle, the posterior margin broadly rounded; nasus slightly thick, shorter than the rest of the head, the lateral outline of the head almost straight. Antennae 13-segmented: segment 1 stout, one fifth wider than segment 2 and more than twice as long; segment 2 the shortest, only slightly shorter than segment 4; segment 3 distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4; segments 4—6 gradually longer, segment 6 equal to segment 3; segments 7 and 8 about as long as segment 6; segments 8—12 gradually shorter, segment 13 distinctly shorter than segment 12. Pronotum of the usual form, the anterior and posterior halves strongly contrasting in colour, anterior margin slightly concave, with sparse long bristles. Legs long and slightly thick, femora with few bristles, claws and tarsi long and slender. Abdomen short and broad, the tergites except the first three far more densely bristled than the rest of the body, some bristles very long. Measurements: body length (varying with the position of the head) 3.00—3.75 mm; head length 1.76—1.82 mm; head width 1.08—1.14 mm; pronotum length 0.20 mm, width 0.55 mm; hind tibia length 1.08 mm. Head colour and size of soldiers vary slightly between colonies.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish, with two broad cinnamon-brown bands on each side of the midline (running from the posterior margin of the frons to the vertex, the outer pair almost reaching the posterior margin, the inner pair shorter and broader); head capsule sutures indistinct; postclypeus and labrum antimony yellow; antennae and legs cream. Head short and broad, widest in the middle, the lateral margins narrowing slightly towards the broadly rounded posterior margin, bristles very few. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 3 almost always distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4; segments 9—13 gradually longer, segment 14 distinctly shorter and narrower. Postclypeus small (0.285×0.570 mm), strongly convex and smooth, the median suture very indistinct; anteclypeus about half the length of the postclypeus. Pronotum similar in shape to that of the soldier but uniformly pale and with shorter bristles. Measurements: body length 4.50 mm; head length (to the end of the labrum) 1.88 mm; head length (to the frontoclypeal suture) 0.91 mm; head width 1.36 mm; pronotum length 0.34 mm, width 0.74 mm; hind tibia length 1.08 mm.
